offers_products.reason: Sells access to online talent marketplaces (Dice, ClearanceJobs) and AI matching tools, which are software-platform products.

offers_services.reason: Recruitment marketplace access and adjacent services, such as recruitment and employer-branding offerings, are core to what it sells.

sells_to_consumers.reason: Employers and recruiters pay. Job seekers use the platforms free, so they aren't the main buyers.

sells_to_organizations.reason: Employers, recruiters and defense contractors such as Lockheed Martin, Leidos and Booz Allen buy job postings and database access.

recurring_revenue.reason: Most revenue comes from recruiter subscription packages on Dice and ClearanceJobs, which are renewed repeatedly.

cyclical_demand.reason: Employers cut recruiting spend and job postings when hiring slows, so Dice and ClearanceJobs subscriptions are easy to reduce.

big_ticket.reason: Recruiters buy job-posting and resume-database subscriptions, which are modest recurring purchases, not large infrequent ones.

people_delivered.reason: Customers pay for platform access, a candidate database and matching technology, not for staff time.

large_customers.reason: Customers are mostly recruiters, staffing firms and employers of many sizes. Large defense contractors are named, but they aren't the whole base.

asset_heavy.reason: Online job marketplaces (Dice, ClearanceJobs) need software and data, not plants, fleets or properties.

notes: The split between large and small customers is uncertain. Revenue is mostly subscription-style recruiter packages.
